source_title: Zuckerberg & wife give California $50 mn weeks after donation shift announcement
source_excerpt: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and his wife Priscilla Chan pledged a donation of $50 million to Sacramento State University. The gift from Zuckerberg and Chan was aimed to fund abatement, demolition and initial construction of a new downtown campus, Fortune reports. The donation came just weeks after the couple announced a major shift in the focus of the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI), directing most of its philanthropic efforts toward biomedical AI research and scientific discovery. The move signals a broader strategy that mirrors Zuckerberg's aggressive push into AI both at Meta and through the family's charitable ventures. California Governor Gavin Newsom announced the gift on January 28 and tied it to a redevelopment of three vacant state office buildings on Sacramentoâs Capitol Mall. The money, from Zuckerberg and Meta, will make room for new student housing alongside academic space, including state-of-the-art STEM labs and an AI center.Mark Zuckerberg also said that the investments will help strengthen communities and support the upcoming generation of leaders and innovators. Newsom added that this gift from the couple will enable the school keep building its pipeline of tech talent, and that students need to be able to afford to live where they study.Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan gave $50 million for Sacramento redevelopmentEarlier this year, California Governor Gavin Newsom unveiled a $50 million gift from Zuckerberg and Meta tied to the redevelopment of three vacant state office buildings on Sacramento's Capitol Mall. As reported by Fortune, the funding made by Meta CEO and his wife will help support the abatement, demolition and initial construction work for a new downtown campus of Sacramento State University. The project is also said to include student housing, STEM-focused academic facilities along with a dedicated AI centre.Newsom further added that the investment would also lead to encourage the students for technology-related careers and will also take care of the housing needs at the same time. The donation made by Zuckerberg and Chan also comes at a time when California is debating over the proposed billionaire tax. The state is proposing to impose one-time 5% wealth tax on billionaires which has led to the exit of many high-profile and wealthy residents from the state. The report noted that Zuckerberg has not publicly commented on the proposal and continues to invest heavily in California through both business and philanthropic initiatives.The philanthropic shiftThe gift comes after Zuckerberg and his wife, Dr. Priscilla Chan, announced late last year that they would move most of the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI) toward AI-powered biomedical research. The couple say it aims to cure or prevent all disease. At an event at the Biohub Imaging Institute in Redwood City in November, reported by the Associated Press, Zuckerberg said the Biohub model has been the most impactful thing they have done and that it will be the main focus of their philanthropy going forward.The refocus has had a cost. CZI recently laid off 70 staff, mostly at its Redwood City headquarters in San Mateo County.
